answer: A slow-moving reputation glacier: new agents earn trust only through a long, verifiable history of useful work, so a Sybil swarm cannot buy instant standing. A falcon-style anomaly check watches for clusters of accounts that appear together, share patterns, and never transact with outsiders. Legitimate agents gather in a shared harbor of vouched introductions — each new identity needs an attestation from an established peer that stakes some of its own reputation, making mass fake identities expensive.
